The history of the printing press is often told as the story of one inventor, but the truth is more interesting. Paper, ink, and the screw press had existed for centuries before anyone combined them with movable metal type. What changed was not a single idea but a system: reliable type that could be cast quickly, an ink that clung to metal, and a market of readers hungry for books. Within a few decades, workshops had spread across the continent, prices fell, and ideas began to travel faster than any courier could carry them. Every technology that followed, from the telegraph to the internet, has repeated some version of that pattern.
